solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Detaching front bit from wall shelf makes loud din

indicators.note: detaching something from the shelf word means taking that piece off it

parts.note: a bracket is a shelf fixed to a wall

indicators.note: the front of the word bit is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone noisily wrenching a shelf off the wall makes a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front bit' is the B at the head of 'bit'; 'Detaching' takes it from BRACKET.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a racket is an uproar or a loud, confused noise.

clue.text: Unprofessional co-worker implicated in a union leader's end

indicators.note: implicated in means caught up within, so the colleague word sits inside the other letters
the end of the word leader is its closing letter

parts.note: a mate is a workmate or fellow worker

explanation.surface: A colleague gets caught up in the downfall of a trade union boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' gives U and 'leader's end' gives R; MATE goes after the A, inside A-U-R.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur does something unpaid, not as a profession, so the word also means unprofessional.

clue.text: Flipping head hit desk: I swayed woozily, completely stunned

indicators.note: flipping turns the slang word for head over, so it is read back to front

parts.note: conk is slang for the head (or nose)

indicators.note: woozily suggests dizzy confusion, so the letters of desk, I and swayed are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone bangs their head on a desk, sways about dizzily and is left dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' turns CONK into KNOC; 'woozily' rearranges DESKISWAYED into KEDSIDEWAYS. 'Hit' just links the halves.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be knocked sideways is to be utterly astonished or overwhelmed.

clue.text: In Rome you'll head study of Italian region

indicators.note: to head is to go in front, so the Italian pronoun comes first

parts.note: tu is the Italian word for you, as spoken in Rome
to scan is to study or examine closely

explanation.surface: A visitor is told that in Rome they will lead a study of an Italian area.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: 'of Italian region' means belonging to Tuscany.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscan means belonging to Tuscany, the central Italian region around Florence.

clue.text: A place to sleep in California? Fantastic!

indicators.note: in places the first pieces within the state abbreviation

parts.note: pit is slang for a bed

explanation.surface: Someone finds a place to sleep in California and is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital as an exclamation is dated British slang for 'excellent!'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned British exclamation of approval meaning excellent or splendid.

clue.text: Rare, cute wild animal

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters of rare and cute are scrambled

explanation.surface: A description of an uncommon, sweet-looking beast living in the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' looks like part of the description but rearranges RARECUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature is any living being, especially an animal.

clue.text: Novel instruction for paver working overtime?

definitions.meaning: a paver lays flagstones, so a busy one would be told to lay down further stones

explanation.surface: A puzzling new order issued to a road worker doing extra hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective (new) but names Evelyn Waugh's wartime satire; 'flags' are paving stones.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Evelyn Waugh's comic novel, and literally an order to lay additional paving stones.

clue.text: More than one choirboy appears afraid to miss mass

indicators.note: to miss means to go without, so the letter for mass drops out

parts.note: someone who trembles shows fear
m is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Nervous choirboys seem too scared to go to Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service but is just M, as in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Trebles are boy sopranos, the highest voices in a church choir, so the plural fits several choirboys.

clue.text: Girl taken into hospital is anaesthetised

indicators.note: the name is held inside the run of letters across these three words

explanation.surface: A girl is admitted to hospital and put under for surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The name straddles hospitaL IS Anaesthetised.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisa is a common female first name, so it serves as an example of a girl.

clue.text: Window cleaners ruined by more hitches, alas

indicators.note: ruined suggests wrecking, so these fifteen letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Window cleaners lament that more snags have spoilt their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' signals rearranging MOREHITCHESALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft chamois leathers are the traditional cloths used to polish glass dry after washing.

clue.text: Note lawyers in US state look smart

parts.note: C is a musical note

indicators.note: in puts the lawyers inside the name of the state

parts.note: Utah is a state of the western USA
DAs are district attorneys, American prosecuting lawyers

explanation.surface: A memo about attorneys based in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sets the lawyers inside the state name, just after its first three letters. DAs are American district attorneys, a usage British solvers may find less familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to cut a dash is to make a stylish, impressive appearance.

clue.text: Slightly alter window, originally having wood frame

indicators.note: a frame surrounds, so the timber word goes around the letter

parts.note: teak is a hardwood

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word window

explanation.surface: Advice on adjusting a window that came with a wooden frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' looks like a noun about the window but tells TEAK to enclose W.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to tweak is to make a small adjustment.

clue.text: Friend keeps turf cultivated with skill

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the friend word contains the other letters

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

indicators.note: cultivated soil is turned over, so the letters of turf are rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend looks after the lawn with skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' looks like a description of the lawn, but it is the anagram signal; 'keeps' then holds the reworked letters inside the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something artfully is doing it cleverly or skilfully.

clue.text: Collection of pots around part of garden

parts.note: c (circa) is the abbreviation for around, used with dates
a rockery is a garden feature of rocks and plants

explanation.surface: A gardener's pots are grouped about the rock garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a placing instruction but is just C, for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Crockery is earthenware dishes and pots taken together.

clue.text: Fish recipe, one filed by cooks

indicators.note: filed by means lined up between, so the two letters sit between the pair

parts.note: to do is to cook, as in doing the vegetables
the plural gives a second copy of the same word
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions
a is one

explanation.surface: A fish recipe passed along by a team of chefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooks' gives two DOs, since each cook 'does' the food; R and A go between them. 'Fish' looks like part of 'fish recipe' but stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The dorado is a large game fish of warm seas, also called the mahi-mahi.

clue.text: I'll give you my word concert is finishing with Queen

indicators.note: finishing with means the royal abbreviation comes at the end

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

explanation.surface: A concert ends with a royal appearance, and someone swears it will.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen. The definition is what such a person might say.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pledges their word is one who makes a pledge, so the phrase describes them in their own voice.

clue.text: A room 'Independent' journalist protected against attack?

parts.note: the clue appears in the Independent, so its own paper is our paper
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper's reporter shut in a room as though under siege.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent' journalist is 'our ED', since the puzzle runs in the Independent.
explanation.definitionFit: Armoured vehicles or ships are plated with metal to shield them from enemy fire.

clue.text: European resort empty? Quite the reverse

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

indicators.note: this asks for the word meaning empty to be read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to drain is to empty

explanation.surface: A traveller asks whether a resort is deserted and is told it is the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the reverse' looks like a reply but turns DRAIN into NIARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard is a native of Spain, a European country.

clue.text: Missionary given job in 'ealthy environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds, so the dropped-aitch word goes around the job

parts.note: hale means healthy, and the apostrophe drops its h
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A missionary posted to a place with a healthy climate.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ealthy marks the lost H, so HALE becomes ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the first Christian missionaries, and the word names any pioneering missionary.

clue.text: Articles by writer include rare Middle Eastern language

indicators.note: include means hold within, so the two articles contain the letter for rare

parts.note: a and a are two indefinite articles
a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: Pieces by an author take in an uncommon Middle Eastern tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author but is a pen, BIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic is the Semitic language spoken across the Arab world.

clue.text: Be impressed ultimately by broadcast about eleven o'clock?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the turned word follows on
ultimately points to the closing letter of impressed
about means turned round, so the word for broadcast is read backwards

parts.note: to emit is to send out or broadcast

explanation.surface: Someone is struck by a late-evening broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns EMIT into TIME. The question mark flags eleven o'clock as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven o'clock is an example of a usual hour for going to sleep.

clue.text: A particular problem for playwright

parts.note: one can mean a particular, as in one day last week
an ill is a trouble or problem

explanation.surface: A particular difficulty facing a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene O'Neill was the American dramatist of Long Day's Journey into Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill is an example of a playwright, a Nobel-winning American dramatist.

clue.text: With amusing entertainment finishing early, admit disappointment

indicators.note: finishing early means stopping before the last letter

parts.note: a comedy is a funny show
to own is to admit or confess

explanation.surface: A funny show ends too soon and the audience confess they are let down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finishing early' cuts the final Y from COMEDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is a loss of status or a letdown, a disappointing anticlimax.

clue.text: Something sweet regularly eaten by foul dog? Yes

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, starting with the first of foul

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a nasty dog eats sweets often, and the answer is yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes' looks like an answer to the question but supplies the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Fudge is a soft confection made from sugar, butter and milk.

clue.text: Board and lodgings, perhaps, in part of a castle

definitions.meaning: one's ... is one's living costs, such as food and a room
the strongest central tower of a castle

explanation.surface: Accommodation offered within a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep means one's upkeep or maintenance, and also the main fortified tower of a castle.

clue.text: Additional foreign cash I obtained in French airport, surprisingly

parts.note: extra means additional

indicators.note: obtained in places the money and the I within the airport name

parts.note: Orly is a Paris airport
the dinar is the currency of several countries, such as Serbia and Jordan

explanation.surface: A traveller is amazed to get extra foreign currency at a Paris airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obtained in' looks like part of the travel story, but it places both the currency and the I inside the airport name.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: extraordinarily means remarkably, in a way that astonishes.

clue.text: Happy and relieved to be given first place

indicators.note: this puts the place abbreviation in front of the relief word

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
eased means relieved or lessened

explanation.surface: A competitor is delighted and relieved to be awarded first place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First place' looks like winning, but 'first' places PL ahead of EASED.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to be pleased is to be glad or contented.

clue.text: Pinching girl, boy's severely punished

indicators.note: pinching means holding tightly, so the boy word grips the girl word

parts.note: a lad is a boy; here the 's stands for is
she stands for a girl or woman

explanation.surface: A boy is harshly punished for pinching a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'boy is pinching girl': LAD holds SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lashed means whipped or flogged, a severe punishment.
